Alaska.Ai — The Stack

No defensible target this cycle.
The 14-day window (May 29 – June 12, 2026) produced zero survivors. The window was broadened to 21 days (May 22 – June 12, 2026) per protocol. Still zero survivors. Nine candidates were evaluated; all failed the anti-confabulation gate. This is a correct outcome — the bar was not lowered.

Mapper Validation Note

14-day window exhausted with zero survivors; broadened to 21-day window (May 22 – June 12, 2026) per protocol. Still zero survivors. C_F1/C_R1 (NRC Part 57 / Oklo Aurora at Eielson AFB): Gate 1 FAILS — POWER Magazine article is dated June 11, 2025 (one year outside both windows, confirmed by WebFetch); ANS Bowen article is March 3, 2026, outside the 21-day window; no independent news outlet article found within either window. Gate 5 would also fail: OAR does not launch until September 2026, so the OAR Director’s Part 57 eligibility determination is not yet an operative institutional chokepoint. C_F2 (Southcentral Alaska Gas-to-Power Bridge): Gate 1 FAILS the verbatim verification test — WebFetch of the Alaska’s News Source June 9, 2026 article confirmed the article is in-window but the verbatim quote attributed to Chugach Electric Association is NOT present; the article does not mention Chugach Electric Association at all. Gate 5 would also fail: FERC (5-member), RCA (5-member), and Chugach Board (cooperative board) all fail the single-actor test; USCG Captain of the Port Anchorage not verifiable by name. C_F3 (FCC SLTE Submarine Cable Blanket License): Gate 1 passes on the Communications Daily article (June 5, 2026, confirmed in-window). Gate 4 FAILS — the fetched article contains zero Alaska-specific content; the SLTE rule is national with no Alaska AI consequence documented in any fetched source. Gate 5 would also fail (5-member Commission vote; FCC IB Chief not verifiable — FCC pages returned HTTP 503). C_V1 (SBIR/STTR Strategic Breakthrough Award): Gate 1 FAILS — article dates are March 16 and April 13, 2026, outside both windows. C_V2 (NSF Regional Innovation Engines): Gate 1 FAILS — September 2025 trigger, outside all windows by more than six months. C_V3 (GCI-Quintillion FCC Section 214 Transfer): Gate 1 FAILS — April 22, 2026 trigger, outside the 21-day window; overlaps with C_F3 which fails Gate 4. C_CS1 (AIDEA Arctic Infrastructure Development Fund — Coastal Plain Lease Capital Stack): Gate 1 PASSES (KMXT June 5, 2026, confirmed real and in-window). Gate 4 FAILS — mechanism is oil and gas lease financing; no AI data center or AI infrastructure consequence documented in any fetched primary source; AI connection is speculative. Gate 5 also FAILS — AIDEA Board majority vote is a committee; AIDF program page documents no individual Executive Director deployment authority. Gate 3 partially FAILS — DEC 18 AAC 87 page returned HTTP 403. Multiple simultaneous gate failures. C_CS2 (CIRI-OSC Global): Gate 1 FAILS — March 8, 2026 trigger, outside both windows. C_CS3 (APFC FY27 IPS / CIO Execution Mechanism): Gate 1 FAILS — BriefGlance.com is a commercial business intelligence service, not an independent news outlet; APFC’s own news page is an agency announcement. Gate 3 also FAILS — Marcus Frampton’s individual binding investment authority is not documented in any fetchable primary source. Gate 5 also FAILS for the same reason. Zero mechanisms pass all seven gates after broadening to 21 days. This is a correct no-target outcome; the bar was not lowered.

Editor’s Note

Run: 2026-06-12 (America/Anchorage) Branch: claude/linkedin-stack-2026-06-12 Window: 14-day primary (May 29 – June 12); broadened to 21-day (May 22 – June 12) per protocol. Scouts: 4 ran in parallel (facilities, vehicles, capital_sovereignty, regulatory). All completed. Mapper: Applied 7-point anti-confabulation gate to 9 merged candidates. Zero survived. Most common failure modes this cycle: 1. Gate 1 (news tie): Many strong mechanisms lack in-window independent news triggers. The POWER Magazine article for NRC Part 57 was June 11, 2025 — one year old. The Gas-to-Power Bridge trigger had a verbatim mismatch (Chugach quote not in article). APFC IPS trigger (BriefGlance) is a commercial intelligence service, not an outlet. 2. Gate 4 (AK AI consequence): The AIDEA ANWR Coastal Plain mechanism passes Gate 1 but the AI connection is speculative — the mechanism is oil/gas lease financing. FCC SLTE order is a national rule with no Alaska-specific content in the trigger article. 3. Gate 5 (chokepoint asymmetry): FERC (5-member), RCA (5-member), FCC Commission (5-member), AIDEA Board (majority vote) — all committee bodies that fail the single-named-individual test. No deviations from protocol other than the standard 21-day window broadening. No subagent stalls. No image rendered (no-target run). Mechanisms to watch for next cycle (good structure, only missing in-window trigger): - NRC Part 57 / Oklo Aurora at Eielson: Watch for news coverage after June 15 comment deadline closes. If OAR launch (September 2026) generates independent news, this mechanism may clear Gate 1 in a future cycle. - CIRI-OSC Global Federal Technology Stack: Watch for a new in-window article covering the OSC subsidiary network and SBA 8(a) freeze impact. The March 2026 trigger is stale. - Southcentral Alaska Gas-to-Power Bridge: The Chugach quote about data centers and gas supply DID appear in a May 5 ADN article (per facilities scout). If new coverage drops with a Chugach official on record after May 29, this mechanism becomes viable. - GCI-Quintillion FCC transfer: Watch for FCC IB decision DA or news coverage of the pending transfer applications (SCL-T/C-20250821-00030 through -00033).
